findings.claim: The diff adds a new test file mcp-server/src/__tests__/loftUrl.test.ts, which is not in the touch-point list; the listed test file mcp-server/src/__tests__/videoFrames.test.ts is not changed by the diff at all.
findings.impact: No user-visible effect: the file is test-only and its tests cite SPEC-CORE-021 as the spec requires. A reader who uses the touch-point list to find the tests for this spec looks in videoFrames.test.ts, finds only the two unchanged SPEC-CORE-008/009 .loft tests, and may conclude the new behavior has no tests or add duplicates there.
findings.evidence: The diff header shows 'new file mode' for mcp-server/src/__tests__/loftUrl.test.ts (138 lines; describe.each over both tools, covering I1, I2, I3, I5 and I6). Nothing in the diff touches videoFrames.test.ts: its .loft tests at videoFrames.test.ts:138 and :440 still assert only the fallback text. The spec's touch-point list names 'mcp-server/src/__tests__/videoFrames.test.ts: the existing .loft test and new tests'.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant names the test file location. Only the touch-point list is inaccurate: the new tests live in a different, unlisted file.

findings.proposed_fix: Record a revision in docs/process/reviews/feature-mcp-loft-url/invariants.md that replaces the videoFrames.test.ts touch point with mcp-server/src/__tests__/loftUrl.test.ts. Alternatively, move the tests into videoFrames.test.ts.

specification_compliance: Production code changes are confined to mcp-server/src/tools/video.ts: the loftError/readLoftUrl helpers, the .loft branch of both handlers and the two descriptions. This matches the listed touch point.
mcp-server/README.md changes only the get_video_frame and list_video_scenes rows, as listed.
docs/specs/mcp-loft-url.md, docs/specs/INDEX.md and docs/process/reviews/feature-mcp-loft-url/* are implicit touch points and are not reported.
readLoftUrl calls client.requestRaw('GET', '/api/files/{id}/stream') with no options, so it sends no Range or X-Lit-Drive header. This is consistent with the drive-boundary pass-through.
In getVideoFrame the .loft check precedes the duration check (video.ts around lines 164-167), consistent with I3.
No touch point outside the list was found in source, backend or addons. The only unlisted place is the new test file loftUrl.test.ts.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A url that contains newlines or very long text is copied verbatim into the error text. This is in scope by the spec's choice: there is no validation under the personal-tool threat model.
regression_risks: Native path: readLoftUrl is reached only inside the mime === LOFT_MIME branch, so native calls send no /stream request. videoFrames.test.ts:613-624 asserts rawCalls is empty for both tools on a native video, which covers I4.
test_coverage: loftUrl.test.ts covers I1 for four providers, a URL containing spaces, a query string and a fragment, and both tools.

loftUrl.test.ts covers I2 and I5 for 404, 410 and 500 stream errors, network and timeout rejections, non-JSON and empty bodies, non-object JSON, and missing, empty, null, numeric and object url values.
loftUrl.test.ts covers I3 (exact request sequence, no intelligence/bytes/SSE call) and the .loft-before-duration ordering (t=5000).
loftUrl.test.ts covers I6 by comparing results for two drive arguments.
videoFrames.test.ts:138 and :440 keep covering the fallback when requestRaw is not stubbed.
